rv.q: The piece, which ran about 110 minutes on opening, needs some cuts and I think Chum still needs to figure out what he wants to do with Ma, just as the production needs to allow the overly frenetic subplot between Sophea and Seth to grow.
Produced to pretty much perfection here, Chum’s work always comes off as specific, involving, highly personal.
BALD SISTERS could definitely use some more tightening when it comes to the specific scenes and overall narrative flow.
With incredible performances across the board, Bald Sisters is must-see theater.
In his 100 minute one-act, Chum presents an emotionally wrenching, yet unexpectedly hilarious, portrait of three women trying to deal with everything that life throws at them.
This show makes you proud to be an American, while at the same time changing your view of what it means to be one.
Ultimately, however, it's Lim's deeply felt, deeply resonant performance as Him, Chum's best-developed, most compelling character, that grounds this play.
Although BALD SISTERS is amusing, it's not endearing. I was primarily left perplexed.
The story and the characters all have potential but they never seem to coalesce into a coherent throughline.
“Bald Sisters” is a masterful portrayal of an immigrant family from Cambodia who struggles to adapt to a new environment, separate and distinct from their country of origin.

cn.t: Critics find this Cambodian-American family drama graceful and well-acted, with universal themes of grief and identity resonating beyond its immigrant story. However, some feel it treads familiar dysfunctional family territory without fully exploring its deeper cultural trauma.
